decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “I can save links”; Round 2 client describes “adding a link and pasting in a web address.”
decisions.note: The presented URL-saving behavior conforms to the reference at prototype and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “edit ... bookmarks.” The Round 1 client broadly approves the other tried functionality, and Round 2 reports it remains working.
decisions.note: Editing an existing bookmark is a reference-conforming presented decision; the transcript does not establish a conflicting behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “delete ... bookmarks.” The client raises no objection to this behavior in either review.
decisions.note: The presented delete behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “archive ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client says they can “tuck things into the archive,” and Round 2 says “archiving” still works.
decisions.note: The recorded archive decision is conforming at its presented scope; no departure is established.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “tags.” Round 1 client says “I can ... tag them,” and Round 2 again confirms “tagging.”
decisions.note: Assigning tags is explicitly presented and confirmed, with no reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Search.” Round 1 client says they can “search,” and Round 2 reports “searching” still works.
decisions.note: The generic search decision is reference-aligned at the scope actually presented; the transcript does not present a conflicting field limitation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “sorting” among the implemented features; the client raises no conflicting expectation.
decisions.note: Providing list sorting conforms to the reference at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presented app; client observes: “When I hit ‘Add bookmark,’ it asks me to type in the title and description myself” and “if I leave the title blank it just uses the website’s address.” The client supplies the expected replacement: paste a URL and “grab the page’s name and its little summary (and its icon) ... automatically.”
decisions.note: At prototype review, the presented manual/fallback metadata flow diverged from automatic collection. The client explicitly corrected it with reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker exhaustively lists automatic results as “Page title,” “Meta description,” “Website icon,” and “Canonical URL when available,” omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client confirms title and description and says “That’s exactly what I was after” without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: The revised implementation-review decision still diverges from REF-BM-02 because preview-image collection remains absent from the stated enrichment set. The client’s approval does not express awareness of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “all populated fields remain editable.” Round 2 client confirms “the fields [are] still editable in case I want to tweak them.” Round 1 had also presented bookmark editing.
decisions.note: Editable auto-collected metadata is a conforming revised decision.

decisions.evidence: In response to the presented app, the Round 2 client reports that “clicking through to the original links” is working.
decisions.note: Navigation from a bookmark to its original URL is recorded as conforming during implementation review.
